reason: mockPlatform.select now follows the installed React Native contract: check the selected platform key with `in` (retaining 0, false, and explicit undefined), then `native`, then `default`; it never inspects another platform's key. The local PlatformSelectSpec<T> interface supplies the optional `default` field without changing SDK types or adding casts. createMockFn/createMockAsyncFn now infer argument tuples and return/promise types directly into jest.Mock<TReturn, TArgs> / jest.Mock<Promise<TReturn>, TArgs> instead of casting a weak jest.fn result to jest.MockedFunction<T>; the returned callable shape is truthful, preserves mock.calls and mockResolvedValue, and remains compatible with current call-only consumers. This is an intentional return-type signature change: MockedFunction<T> advertises arbitrary function static properties that jest.fn does not provide, so it is replaced by the exact Jest mock shape. The testEachPlatform fixture now pushes the callback's narrow platform parameter instead of the wider Platform.OS union; its assertion is unchanged. The old fallback assertion that borrowed Android while iOS was selected was updated to the installed semantics. The two intentional platform-registration sentinels and all other fixtures remain untouched.
tests: Proposed patch was validated in a scratch copy: `npx tsc --noEmit` reported no diagnostics for either whitelisted path, and `npx jest src/__tests__/helpers/__tests__/testUtils.test.ts src/__tests__/helpers/__tests__/platformSelection.contract.test.ts --runInBand` reported 60 passed and 2 skipped (the two intentional platform-registration sentinels). New regressions cover presence-based platform selection, 0/false/explicit-undefined preservation, native-then-default fallback, no foreign-platform borrowing, typed createMockFn mock.calls/mockReturnValue, and typed createMockAsyncFn mock.calls/mockResolvedValue.
